title: Impact
text:
The Halcyon came down hard, skidding across grey dust for nearly a kilometer before the hull finally caught on a ridge of black rock and stopped.

Mira Okafor unbuckled with hands that wouldn't quite stop shaking and pulled herself toward the console. Half the board was dark. The half that wasn't kept insisting, calmly, that the ship was fine.

"ORSA," she said. "Full damage report."

ORSA: Hull integrity at sixty-one percent. Primary reactor offline. Life support nominal for one hundred forty hours at current crew count.

Tobias Lin: One hundred forty hours. Great. Plenty of time to figure out how we're not going to die here.

Mira Okafor: We're not going to die here. We're going to fix the reactor.

Tobias Lin: With what? My devastating charm?

Mira didn't answer. She was already staring at a line on the console she hadn't asked ORSA about — a signal, structured, repeating, coming from somewhere on the surface below them. It had started four minutes before impact.
